title: A Simple Judgment Method for Joint Action of Antibacterial Agents on Bacterial Resistance
author: Tang, Tong, et al.

steps.title: Prepare E. coli inoculum
steps.instruction: Grow a preculture of E. coli MG1655 K‑12 in LB broth (1 % w/v tryptone, 0.5 % w/v yeast extract, 1 % w/v NaCl, pH 7.0–7.2) at 37 °C, 180 rpm for 6 h; dilute the culture ~10⁵‑fold to obtain an inoculum of ≈5 × 10⁴ cells mL⁻¹ for subsequent assays.

steps.title: Create antibacterial concentration series
steps.instruction: Prepare serial dilutions of each test antibacterial agent with equal log‑dose intervals (typically 12–16 points for toxicity, 10–12 points for conjugation). Set the lowest and highest concentrations based on a preliminary experiment so that the series spans from no effect (0 % inhibition) to maximal inhibition.

steps.title: Set up microplate toxicity assay
steps.instruction: In each well of a 96‑ or 100‑well transparent microplate add 80 µL of the antibacterial dilution, 80 µL MH broth (3 % w/v beef infusion, 1.75 % w/v casein hydrolysate, 0.15 % w/v water‑soluble starch, pH 7.2–7.4), and 40 µL E. coli inoculum (total 200 µL). For control wells replace the 80 µL antibacterial solution with 80 µL of 1 % w/v NaCl. Perform 3–5 replicates per condition.

steps.title: Incubate and measure growth
steps.instruction: Incubate the microplate at 37 °C with 180 rpm shaking for 24 h. Measure OD₆₀₀ of each well with a microplate reader. Calculate inhibition % using Inhibition (%) = (OD₆₀₀,c − OD₆₀₀,t) / OD₆₀₀,c × 100 % and generate the dose‑response curve.

steps.title: Determine mutation frequency
steps.instruction: Repeat the toxicity microplate assay (steps above) for the mutation test, then:

substeps.instruction: Collect the 200 µL from each replicate well into a 1.5 mL tube; wash the cells three times with 1 % w/v NaCl (centrifuge 3 min at 6000 rpm, discard supernatant, vortex 5 s, add 1 mL NaCl each wash) and resuspend in the same saline.
Dilute ≤10 µL of the suspension ≈10⁶‑fold with 1 % NaCl to enumerate total CFU; concentrate the remaining suspension ≈3‑fold to enumerate mutant CFU.

Plate the diluted suspension on antibiotic‑free LB agar (1.5–2 % agar) and the concentrated suspension on LB agar containing rifampicin 25 mg L⁻¹; incubate 12–15 h and count colonies to obtain CFU mL⁻¹ for total and mutant cells.
Calculate mutation frequency MF = CFU_mut / CFU_total and promotion % = (MF_t − MF_c) / MF_c × 100 %; use at least two duplicates.

steps.title: Assess conjugative transfer frequency
steps.instruction: Perform the conjugation assay as follows:

substeps.instruction: Culture donor E. coli (RP4) and recipient E. coli (Nal) in LB broth with their respective antibiotics at 37 °C, 180 rpm for 6 h.
Wash each culture three times with 1 % NaCl (centrifuge 3 min at 6000 rpm, vortex 5 s, add 1 mL NaCl each wash) and adjust both OD₆₀₀ to 0.5 with saline.
Mix donor and recipient at a 1:2 ratio, shake 20 min at 180 rpm, then shake an additional 20 min; the mixed inoculum should be ≈5 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹.
Prepare serial dilutions of the antibacterial agent (10–12 log‑spaced points; concentration range set by preliminary experiment).

In a 1.5 mL tube add 40 µL antibacterial dilution, 100 µL 2‑fold diluted LB broth, and 60 µL mixed inoculum (total 200 µL). For the control replace the 40 µL agent with 40 µL 1 % NaCl. Perform 3–5 replicates.

Incubate the mixture for 12 h at 37 °C (mating). Dilute the suspension ≈10⁵‑fold with 1 % NaCl and plate on: (a) LB agar with nalidixic acid 40 mg mL⁻¹ (recipients) and (b) LB agar with nalidixic acid 40 mg mL⁻¹ + kanamycin 40 mg mL⁻¹ (transconjugants). Incubate (typically 12–15 h) and count CFU mL⁻¹.
Calculate conjugative transfer frequency CTF = CFU_transconjugant / CFU_recipient and promotion % = (CTF_t − CTF_c) / CTF_c × 100 %; use at least two duplicates.

steps.title: Fit data and design antibacterial mixtures

substeps.instruction: If the growth inhibition curve shows no hormesis, fit with the built‑in DoseResp function; if hormesis is present, fit with the Hormesis function (y = C − D + m/(1 + (x/a)ᵇ) + D/(1 + (x/p)ᵠ)). For mutation and transfer assays use the inverted Hormesis function.
From the fitted toxic curves obtain the median effective concentration (EC₅₀) for each antibacterial agent.

Design a mixed antibacterial solution based on the equitoxic ratio of the individual EC₅₀ values; prepare serial dilutions of the mixture with equal log intervals, setting the concentration range (lowest = no effect, highest = max effect) according to a preliminary experiment.

Determine the effects of the mixture on mutation frequency and conjugative transfer frequency using the exact procedures described in Steps 4–6, and fit these dose‑response data with the inverted Hormesis function.
Extract the concentrations that produce an initial 10 % promotion of mutation (MC₁₀) and of transfer (CTC₁₀) from the fitted curves; these values serve as risk‑threshold parameters.
Compute the Mutation Unit (MU) and Conjugative Transfer Unit (CTU) using:
MU = Σ_i (c_i / MC₁₀,i) and CTU = Σ_i (c_i′ / CTC₁₀,i),

where c_i (or c_i′) are the concentrations of component i in the mixture when the overall mixture reaches MC₁₀ (or CTC₁₀), and MC₁₀,i (CTC₁₀,i) are the single‑component thresholds obtained from the fitted curves.

Compare each index to the thresholds 0.8 and 1.2: MU or CTU < 0.8 indicates synergism, 0.8 ≤ value ≤ 1.2 indicates additive (no interaction), and > 1.2 indicates antagonism of the joint resistance effect.
